title: Lamar Jackson Building Rapport at OTAs | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: Lamar Jackson was back on the practice field Tuesday as the Ravens OTAAS roll on. He's been a fixture throughout the offseason program and Tuesday he was able to get onfield work with the new rookie class. Building rapport with his new receivers Jacobe Lane and Elijah Serat as well as tight ends Matthew Hibner and Josh Quas will be crucial to prepare the rookies well for training camp. And first round pick Vena Awan has been excited to team up with his new quarterback. >> Oh man, I thought about it a lot. You know, his name is a big name around the game. Has been around the game for a little while now. He's a very talented player, phenomenal player. You know, it's going to be a big honor for me and a blessing for me to, you know, block for somebody like that. So, taking a lot of pride in that. >> Everything elevates when number eight is on the field and the energy he's brought this off season has been infectious. Head coach Jesse Mentor said last week that he and Lamar have been in communication throughout and Wednesday's practice will be open to the media and Mentor and players will address the media at the conclusion of that practice. Those pressers will be available to stream on our YouTube, Facebook app, and website. Thanks for watching. We'll be back with you tomorrow.

title: Davison Igbinosun Met With The Media After Practice | Buffalo Bills
text: They saw you have a pick today in practice. What were you looking at and and how did that come about? Um, got an out route. Drove two steps to the man. What's it been like for you going into your first off season here in the NFL just kind of adjusting to that? Just trying to pick the game and soak the game up from them so when I get my opportunity to go out on the field, I'm ready. What's Max been talking to you cuz a year ago he was in your shoes but now he's in this position. title: T.J. Sanders On Preparing At OTAs | Buffalo Bills
text: What was last year like for you? I mean, the injury, change of positions, you know, the second round pick, I'm sure there's expectations, yourself, the team. How difficult a year was that for you last year? >> Uh, I feel like it was a lot of growing pains, you know, um, coming in, you know, um, felt like I was building on something I had found early on before the injury. And um you know that kind of just took me out of my head you know and know being come being able to come back you know uh get told you're going to play DN it's kind of like oh man like okay you know trying to pick that up learn all the things that DNS have you know coming in I just feel like it was honestly a testament of you know my hard work and the things I had to give up and uh bring in um come back cuz like like that injury I thought it was worse than what it was but it wasn't as bad as the doctors were telling me but when I came back you know it was always that uh am I going to be all right factor um can I still do this? Can I still do that? So, just coming back, getting my feet back under me, I feel like was the biggest thing I can grow on >> because you did have that experience at that switching positions, how much will that help you in this new defense and how you fit? >> I feel like it uh it'll help a lot, you know, being able to go outside, inside, having some experience in in this league doing that uh be big for me. >> What did you learn about yourself, all those things you went through, all that experiences? What What did you find out about maybe the person you are, maybe the person you need to be to stay in this league? Um, I feel like honestly, um, just having a more like from my from when I got to the league up until that point, just having a more consistent approach with the things I've done, you know, on the field or off. Um, just having every day a built-in routine that can really like prevent those type of nagging things from really hind me. >> How much does this year feel different from like rookie season, probably your head spinning to now having a year in the league under your belt? >> Uh, I definitely feel like I came in coming in much more confidence. You you just talked about like kind of the mental strain that it had. Have you gone through something like that in your career before? >> No, never never had knee problems. >> So, what was just the challenge of kind of figuring out how to to battle that that mentality of push yourself, you know, past and through the rehab? title: Dave Canales evaluates the opening week of OTAs | Carolina Panthers
text: All right, what a great day getting back on the grass. Something we've been waiting for. Um, three weeks of our phase two, not going at each other uh in the practice. A lot of individual periods, a lot of teaching, different modes, uh tempo on both sides, and now we get to kind of put it all into uh into play. And you know, the biggest challenge, which I'm really proud of the group, is to capture the intensity and the speed of play that we need, but also uh taking care of each other. And that's what I saw today. I saw guys making great decisions um at the line of scrimmage on the ball around the pocket. Obviously um this time of year we don't want people around the quarterback and so there were some good rushes and guys peeled off. Um and then on the in the back half, you know, in the secondary and the linebackers making some plays on the ball where I said, "Hey, look, if you have a clear path to the bath uh to the to the ball, you can make that play. Let's just stay away from those collisions and and a lot of the things that we're not looking for at this time of year." And I thought the guys captured it and were able to uh get some quality football done today. Dave, >> speaking of intensity, we've heard about Bryce Young's total presence. Today, we got to actually hear a little bit of it. What are some of the ways that you feel like he's grown as a leader? I know this is just a couple days into OTAAS. >> Yeah, just total command of the system and knowing what he's looking for, the timing of things, and the more that he owns it, the more he's looking for specific things out of the tight ends, white outs, and backs as the concepts uh come alive. And you know, I heard him get a little bit passionate about, you know, we we got a little bit of a monsoon for a second there in practice. And um you know, once the rain had passed, he was like, "Hey, let's lock back in. We got to come up with these balls." And I think he said it a little more colorful language than that. But um but you know, I just love it. I love the fact that he's taking ownership and the guys see that and and rally around that and something that they all appreciate. >> Hey Dave, what's up with Bobby Brown, T-Mac, and Stone Force? Yeah. So, um, Bobby got a calf, uh, a couple of weeks ago and he's doing great. He's in return to play. Um, he's really close to being back out there. We got to be smart with that stuff. These aren't things that we want to linger. Uh, similar thing for uh, for T-Mac. You know, he had he had some some foot soreness. It wasn't anything alarming, but again, at this point, you know, we don't want things to kind of build up to turn into some type of a nagging, you know, chronic type of deal. And so we just decided to to keep them kind of back them off and and make sure it's the right time to get them back in because we know once they start competing out there, you start you forget you forget what's happening in your body and you're just going and competing and and we want those guys to to feel fully healthy and fully ready to go and hopefully we can get them back out here in the next uh week or two. >> What about Stone? >> Uh Stone Stone was a was uh they just had a baby this weekend. Got a picture. We got a healthy baby, the foresight. So, uh, congrats to them and, um, he shot me a text and a picture and and so really fired up for him and his family. >> Dave, um, what do you expect from AJ Dylan this year? >> Yeah, AJ's got a great opportunity to compete, and there's more than one way to help this team. You know, there's not just running the ball, there's pass protection, there's um, whether it's route running, there's special teams, and these are all things that AJ has had uh, practice and experience in, and so he brings another just uh, veteran player into that room, which is a competitive room. And so we just expect him to show up every day, compete, and uh we'll we'll see where all that plays out. >> Dave, staying in the uh running back room. >> How refreshing and fun was it to see Jonathan Brooks out there in 11s? >> I mean, it it brings me a lot of joy to be able to see him out there. Uh didn't see any hesitation. Just a lot of speed and and decisiveness and how he ran the ball today and got him in the perimeter on a screen and and made some good yards on on one of our screens today. Just uh and not just me, but I think his teammates would say the same thing. They would be up here saying the same thing. just really excited to see Jonathan be out there and do what he loves to do. >> Has he added bulk to his frame? >> Uh I don't know that. I don't know that for sure. I know he's been training like crazy. He looks good, you know, so I don't know exactly pound-for-pound what that looks like, but um he's still moving well and and that's what we want from our guys. We're not really necessarily focused on a certain uh weight, right? It's about being your fastest, strongest that you can operate. And um he certainly looks that right now. >> He was wearing a sleeve. Do you expect him to wear that throughout training camp and stuff like this? >> I'm not sure. Yeah, >> you mentioned guys taking care of each other. We did see one play uh where Devin took Tommy down during the pass. >> Yeah, >> we've heard that Devin is an intense dude. Like his teammates in Jacksonville have mentioned that. Um have you seen that like up close and personal now? >> Well, I think what I've seen from uh from Devin is just being in the right place at the right time and that play in particular was a stick route. You know, Tommy ran a stick route. He made a break on it and Tommy kind of slipped. So it it it looked like a collision a little bit, but I didn't really see that as his intent was wasn't to knock him over. It just kind of happened that way. But what I have seen from Devin is just conscientiousness, communication, and and really being in the right place at the right time. >> Dave, I'm sure you're looking forward to the indoor facility. But early on in this in this OTAA process, do you want to get a feel of sort of how those guys respond to adversity if it's like a monsoon or >> I mean, what a tease, right? We got this beautiful structure going up right in right in our background, you know, and we and we get this heavy rain, which is something that we can make a decision, you know, someday to be able to go in there and and still have a clean practice. The practice got a little bit sloppy during RVA's um you know, just with the with the wet ball. But again, we may play in the rain at some point. You know, um it's been raining when we've gone down to Tampa. We've had rain games here and guys have to go through, do I wear my gloves? Do I take them off and switch them for a different pair? Um different things like that. So, it just causes the guys to focus a little bit. Is Trevan not cleared for contact? Is that why he wore red? >> Yes. So, Trevan is doing great. Um, he had a procedure after the season. He's fully strong. All those things, we want to be smart about that. And just the red jersey just creates an awareness as the linemen are coming to block at the second level. Let's just make sure be smart. Trevan knows as well just to kind of fit his area, be in position, but also be smart. And so, it's just another lay of level of protection. Was that the additional surgery to the one he had at the end of the season? >> Uh, no. It was the same one. >> Shoulder. >> Dave, about Daryl Bevel being in the coaching staff now, the impact that he's had so far for you and and your rest of the staff and the players. >> It's been great. Um, lots of great reminders for me as the head coach. Looking for things things schematically. Um, as Brad's running the practice, you know, we have Daryl back there kind of seeing the whole picture and, you know, just bringing up little things, things about alignment, things about splits, things about, uh, the timing of different concepts, and then just bringing um, a lot of experience from a few different places and some some things, some wrinkles that we're able to factor into our systems, but he's been phenomenal this spring. >> Dave, Jaylen, Jaylen took a huge step last year, obviously captured that number two spot. What are you, what are you looking for for him this year? What do you want to see him develop on and and possibly with him? >> He looks great. Um, he looks fit. He's attacking the ball just like we know that he can. The big thing for him is for he and Bryce to really just continue to take steps in terms of chemistry, you know, as as as Jaylen over the last couple of years has had, you know, pockets of time where he's he's had to deal with things from a physical standpoint. the more we can just have them on the field, the anticipation that happens, knowing what he's doing at the top of his route, knowing where Bryce expects him to be, that's that's my big hope for Jaylen and for Bryce is to continue to build off of that chemistry. >> Jim Gates was working with the linebackers in practice. I know his title hasn't changed, but how is his responsibility shifting after you hired the defensive special teams assistant? Yeah. So, it's a developmentally minded staff and we're always looking for opportunities for guys to grow and we have an opportunity here where Pete's coached our inside linebackers, but Pete's also taking a bigger role with the Gerro and um on the defensive side in terms of the what he can bring from a schematic standpoint, but in this transition, you know, it's a great opportunity for Darren to get with Pete and to kind of just pick his brain to see what he does for individual drills, how he sets up the part to hole to understand where you fit in, when a tight end moves or um different situations and and so this is a great opportunity for Darren while he'll still be helping out on special teams with Tracy. >> Dave, initial assessment on Rasheed who looked to be taking most of the reps alongside Damen. >> Yeah, Rasheed an experienced player um has familiarity with our system. Maybe the words might be a little slightly different uh from Matt Laflur's system in Green Bay, but a lot of carryover, a lot of great communication having another veteran player like Damen playing next to him right there. He's done a great job so far. And again, you know, we're going to let these guys compete, you know, and Monroe's going to have a chance to compete. And um right now, you know, with just the way that we're we're doing things, you know, Rasheed's out there with the first group. Uh Monroe's got a couple of reps with the first group as well, but I'd can't wait to see that play out as we go into camp. >> You mentioned what about the benefits of having a guy like Damen next to him? >> Yeah, it's fantastic because Damen's been in our system for a long time, whether it was in Seattle and now here, his third season in Carolina. um to have him communicate, call out, you know, as the calls come from the center. Luke did a great job today of just getting us aligned properly and getting all the points the right way and protection in the run game, but it echoes out inside out. And so having Damen there with a lot of experience, I'm sure creates a lot of ease for Rasheed, just hearing the right words come out, uh which will help that development. >> With Bobby and Turk out of the mix, what has Kim Jackson shown you these last few weeks in the program, but just overall what his tenure? I'm fired up to see what Cam does with it with this with this opportunity as well as Lee Hunter who just got here. And these are young guys that are big and extremely talented and I can't see can't wait to see that competition in the interior of our defensive line play out. Um especially as Bobby's waiting to come back out there. These guys are getting valuable reps playing next to Derek, you know, and the comp communication that happens and also with the stunts just with Nick and with Pat Jones and Jaylen, you know, and being able to talk through those things. And so invaluable time right now for these guys to be able to grow. >> Impressions of Jaylen and Devin being part of this defense as well. >> It's it's really fantastic to see experienced guys come in. They pick up the system. Jaylen's been in a very similar system before in his time in Miami. Um and then just to be able to see him really just take to the coaching, uh developing that rapport. I've heard the guys have gotten together a couple of times on their own just to break bread. I know he was going to hang out with Pat this past weekend. I didn't Pat Jones. I didn't get a chance to ask if they actually did that, but I love seeing all of that. They understand what it takes to build a team, to be a part of a team that connects and that plays together, not just on the field, but also off the field. And so, I'm really glad that Devin and Jaylen are here to bring that kind of leadership. >> Dave, back on the >> a couple more, >> back on the Bryce Young leadership question. First OTAAS without Andy Dalton, three new quarterbacks into this new system. How has the How has his OTAAS been different than the three previous ones? Well, I'll just talk about uh Kenny and talk about Will Greer right now. Two veteran players, guys that have experience being around a couple of different quarterback rooms. In fact, they were together in Philly uh for a little while and they talk about their time together and and how much they enjoyed working together and they're bringing that camaraderie into that room um for Bryce, you know, so it just adds to the flavor. And then of course having Hannes King in there, a rookie who's learning all these things, he's done a great job of just being being able to connect with those guys. And um I can't say enough about what Will and what Kenny have meant to just, you know, um not just being a support of Bryce. When you build a quarterback room, those guys primary job is to know what they're doing, but also to bring value to the quarterback, to Bryce. And that's really all of our responsibility. And um and I love that Haynes gets to see that happen in front of him by veteran guys who understand their role and understand that you bring value. Even if you're not out there getting the reps, there's so much that you can bring in terms of your experience, uh, watching film, studying other teams, and just, uh, enriching the conversations that happen in there. >> Coach, how do you evaluate the rookies in early in May and early June when they are sharing the field with established veterans and how they can earn the trust from the coaching staff? Yeah, the first part is to just see how we practice, the speed and intensity of which we ask our guys to play with, how we finish plays, how guys chase the ball, the effort, all the things that we see as our standard for the guys that have been here for a while. The young guys get to see that firsthand and then try to apply that effort first. Can you play hard every down? Can you give everything you have? And then you can see sometimes they're not sure exactly what to do. Ask somebody, you know, and and that's where the communication piece comes into play. Um, but we are asking them, you know, and the first thing that we told this group is we're not slowing down for you. You have to go. You have to study. You have to continue to chase to catch up with the information that's in front of you that the guys that have been around have. And uh, it's a challenge to them. And then also, I like to share with them, you also got to have a lot of grace for the mistakes you will make. Those are going to happen. But every day, stack those lessons and find new mistakes to make so you can continue to grow so that we can trust them. But first and foremost, it comes from effort. And I'm really proud of this group. I'm proud of the way that they've applied themselves in the classrooms, hearing great reports on the defense and offensive side. And then of course for me to be able to see it happen on the field. I'm sure I'll go back and watch film and I'll be able to talk to a guy or two about a way they could have finished maybe a little bit faster, a little bit harder, something like that. So um those things will come up and we'll bring them along and uh and uh we'll we'll expect them to be able to contribute in some way or shape or form. >> Without the coordinator duties, how have things changed for you at this first OTAA practice? It just frees me up to bounce around and just see what's happening at different positions and and you know go and hear what Pat McFerson is doing down with the tight ends for a second and you know get with Todd Wash with the defensive line and watch those guys work and just to really get an appreciation for the staff that we have that pushes our groups. I was really looking forward to that. Also just being able to be available to Tracy during special teams and hopping into drills kind of over the last couple of weeks, grabbing a bag, being a part of what they're doing and and really just to like so that every area of our team knows I care about them. I care that we have a high standard for how we're working. It matters to me. So that no group really feels like they're not getting that attention. And I'll be honest, whichever group I go around, there's a little bit of an uptick in terms of the effort and what they're doing. The guys are always competing and I love that. So, I love just kind of being that presence and and supporting the coaches as they as they uh do their thing. >> Are you feel weird? >> It does. You know, kind of like sometimes I'm not sure what to do with my hands, you know, and you know, if I ever feel like that, I just kind of, you know, beline over to another group and and try to add a little juice and a little bit of excitement with what they're doing. And um I like that role and I'm I'm um I'm confident in our coordinators and the the the job that they've done organizing this off season and crescendoing to this point where we get to be on the field and then just continuing to push the group. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Just the shield or whatever it is. Just any way I can help in a drill, uh I'll pop in there and and uh anyway I can. So >> no, I think they're very respectful of that. So >> thank you coach. >> Yeah. All right. Thank y'all.
